plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: Violet-blue spikes ripple across the sun-baked plateaus of Provence in long, perfumed rows. The air hums with bees and smells sweet, herbal and warm.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late June to early August, with peak bloom in mid-July
plants.funFact: Lavender is a member of the mint family. Its flowers have been used for centuries to scent linen, soap and perfume.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: The largest flower head in the protea family looks like a crown of silky pink bracts around a downy center. It opens in the cool, wet months of the Southern Hemisphere winter, when much of the world's garden color is fading.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mainly winter and spring, June to October
plants.location: Fynbos of the Western Cape, South Africa
plants.funFact: King protea is South Africa's national flower. It belongs to a lineage that dates back tens of millions of years, and it is adapted to regrow after wildfires.

plants.name: Echinacea purpurea
plants.description: Rose-purple petals droop around a spiky, copper-orange cone. Butterflies and goldfinches gather at the flower heads in summer meadows and gardens.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring through late summer, so it is in full swing in July
plants.location: Eastern and central North America, in prairies and gardens
plants.funFact: The name Echinacea comes from the Greek word for hedgehog. It refers to the prickly central cone.
